name: Ketovore
lead: Ketovore is an informal label for a ketogenic, very low-carbohydrate diet that centers on meat and other animal foods while allowing some low-carbohydrate plant foods. It sits between a standard ketogenic diet and the carnivore diet, which allows only animal products [1][2]. People adopt it to get leaner, which makes muscle definition and the jawline and face look sharper, and some report clearer skin and steadier energy for training.

The ketogenic diet is a high-fat, adequate-protein, low-carbohydrate diet used in conventional medicine mainly for drug-resistant epilepsy [2]. The carnivore diet gained social-media attention from 2018, when former orthopaedic surgeon Shawn Baker promoted it, and Jordan Peterson and his daughter Mikhaila became prominent followers [1]. Ketovore is described by its followers as a less restrictive version of that approach.
Dietetic bodies such as the British Dietetic Association classify the carnivore diet as a fad diet [1]. No clinical trial of a diet specifically called ketovore has been published.

angle.text: Followers use ketovore eating to lose fat, with a leaner face and more visible muscle as the intended result. Studies of low-carbohydrate diets in general report somewhat more weight loss than low-fat diets in the short term, with the difference narrowing over time.

paras: The term is used informally rather than defined by a medical body. It generally denotes a keto diet in which animal foods dominate and a limited set of low-carbohydrate plants is included. A related variant, the animal-based diet, adds fruit, honey and raw dairy to carnivore eating [1].
On T Nation, one member described adopting a food list as "basically Ketovore" for a body-composition phase, cooking in bulk to control calories [3].

Wikipedia reports that low-carbohydrate diets can produce somewhat more weight loss than low-fat diets in the short and medium term, that the advantage fades over time, and that a 2022 Cochrane review found no benefit at two years compared with balanced diets [5]. When calorie intake is held constant, body-fat change does not appear to differ much with large shifts in fat versus carbohydrate, according to the Endocrine Society as summarized there [5].

A 2025 cross-sectional study of 21 adults who reached type 2 diabetes remission through diet and exercise recorded that 14% followed a "ketovore/carnivore" diet and 52% a low or very low carbohydrate diet; it examined glucose profiles and did not test ketovore for appearance [4].

Wikipedia reports that carnivore eating excludes fruit and vegetables, is low in fiber, can raise LDL cholesterol, and has been called potentially dangerous by dietitians and physicians [1]. In clinical use of ketogenic diets, reported adverse effects include constipation, raised blood lipids and kidney stones, and the diet is started under medical supervision [2]. Low-carbohydrate diets are also associated with constipation, headache, bad breath and cramps in a summarized meta-analysis, and long-term use with higher LDL cholesterol [5].

On T Nation, a lifter reported that however much they tried carnivore, keto, ketovore or low carb, adding carbohydrates and calories back improved recovery and how they felt [6]. This sits alongside other members who use the pattern for cutting phases [3].
No studies found on a diet specifically called ketovore. Related studies cover ketogenic and low-carbohydrate diets generally [2][5].

timeline.event: Shawn Baker promotes the carnivore diet on social media.[1]

lore.intro: Ketovore comes up in T Nation training logs as a cutting-phase eating pattern and as a diet some lifters tried and left.

claims.claim: Ketovore eating supports a leaner physique
claims.believers: Members describe using a ketovore-style food list to control calories during a fat-loss phase [3].
claims.experts: Reviews of low-carbohydrate diets report modest short-term extra weight loss that fades by two years, and no clear difference in fat loss at equal calories [5].

claims.claim: Very low carbohydrate eating helps recovery
claims.believers: Some followers expect better energy and recovery from keto-style eating.
claims.experts: One T Nation lifter reported recovering better after adding carbohydrates back [6]. No trial has tested recovery on a ketovore diet.

card.summary: Keto with a meat-first bias and a few plants allowed; a hybrid label with no trials of its own.
card.note: Neighbouring carnivore diet is described by dietitians as a fad diet with nutrient and lipid concerns.

quick.overview:
Ketovore blends keto and carnivore: mostly meat and animal fat, very low carbohydrate, with a small selection of plant foods. The name is informal.

No clinical trials have tested it for body composition or appearance. Evidence comes from studies of the broader ketogenic diet.
quick.mechanism: Cutting carbohydrate pushes the liver to produce ketone bodies as an alternative fuel, which is the basis of the ketogenic diet. Followers say adding a few plants offers variety and fibre while keeping the meat focus.
quick.risks: Ketogenic diets can cause constipation, raised blood lipids and kidney stones, and medical supervision is advised in clinical use. Dietetic bodies caution about the carnivore end of the spectrum, citing low fibre and higher LDL cholesterol.
